answer: A prism defence splits trust into independent facets - compute contributed, data served, and peer interactions sustained - instead of one score an attacker can buy or copy. Each facet is verified by a different subsystem, is non-transferable, and decays without continued work, so a new identity must earn all of them at once. A sybil farm can fake one facet, like a comet flashing briefly, but cannot sustain every facet across many accounts: the cost multiplies with each identity, while an agent on its own island of steady work passes cheaply because its history is real.
